# Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost — facts

## Definitions

- [statement] The mongodb-atlas-local image is an evaluation and CI option, not a production exit target: MongoDB describes it as single-node without high availability and directs production users to separate supported deployment paths. Local query success alone does not validate a production migration. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/ · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/limitations.md

## Structure and components

- [statement] Moving database documents does not establish application portability: Databasezy explicitly excludes Atlas Search indexes and triggers from its Atlas copy workflow, while MongoDB documents Atlas database Triggers as a separate serverless execution layer. Treat service replacement as a separate exit-work item. (medium confidence) — https://docs.databasezy.com/migrate/providers/mongodb-atlas.html · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md
- [statement] Atlas database Triggers run outside the database server on a serverless compute layer, consume change streams, and invoke Atlas Functions or forward events to AWS EventBridge. Exporting collection data alone does not reproduce that execution service; this exit implication is an architectural inference from the documented design. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost
- [statement] Atlas database Triggers execute in a separate serverless layer over change streams. Combined with migration tools omitting triggers, this implies that an Atlas exit must separately replace or redeploy trigger-dependent application behavior. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost · also: https://docs.databasezy.com/migrate/providers/mongodb-atlas.html

## How it works

- [statement] A practical exit assessment should inventory Search operators and index definitions, trigger functions and schedules, and the operational services the destination must supply. This is a methodological inference from documented feature exceptions and migration omissions. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/limitations.md · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost · also: https://docs.databasezy.com/migrate/providers/mongodb-atlas.html, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/triggers/database-triggers.md
- [statement] The documented feature boundary remains uneven: $rerank is Atlas-only. An application using that stage needs an alternative implementation when leaving Atlas; Percona describes its alternative as a plan. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/limitations.md · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/the-open-way-of-percona-search-for-mongodb/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Databasezy documents its Atlas migration as a copy-only mongodump-to-mongorestore workflow, without continuous synchronization, and explicitly says it does not copy Search indexes or triggers. This limitation describes that migration tool; it does not prove those features are intrinsically impossible to recreate elsewhere. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-28) — https://docs.databasezy.com/migrate/providers/mongodb-atlas.html · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Search and Vector Search are no longer categorically Atlas-only. MongoDB documents self-managed Community and Enterprise deployment paths; its mongot repository offers a Community Search image. Percona independently reports that self-managed search reached GA in July 2026 and describes its downstream Technical Preview. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-07) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/ · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongot/blob/main/README.md, https://www.percona.com/blog/the-open-way-of-percona-search-for-mongodb/
- [statement] The self-managed limitations documentation lists $search, $searchMeta, $vectorSearch, and Search index helper methods as available on both platforms, but lists $rerank as Atlas-only, excludes nestedRoot index syntax on self-managed mongot, and notes differences in $listSearchIndexes output. Portability therefore requires checking the exact feature surface. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/limitations.md · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost
- [statement] Leaving managed Search transfers operational work to the operator. MongoDB assigns provisioning, upgrades, security patching, alerting, logs, recovery supervision, and capacity management to self-managed deployments; Percona separately identifies gaps in the surrounding automation and observability. These are concrete engineering tasks, not a universal dollar estimate for exit. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-07) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/limitations.md · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/the-open-way-of-percona-search-for-mongodb/
- [statement] Search is no longer categorically Atlas-only: MongoDB publishes self-managed mongot deployment paths and source code, and Percona distributes the same underlying engine independently. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/ · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongot/blob/main/README.md, https://www.percona.com/blog/the-open-way-of-percona-search-for-mongodb/
- [statement] MongoDB documents $search, $searchMeta and $vectorSearch on both platforms. Moving off Atlas therefore does not inherently require replacing the search engine; compatibility still needs workload testing. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/limitations.md · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/
- [statement] mongot is source-available under SSPL v1. Percona uses the same license and explicitly distinguishes it from OSI-approved open source; self-hostability alone does not establish unrestricted hosted-service redistribution rights. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongot/blob/main/README.md · keywords: Atlas-only feature lock-in and exit cost · also: https://www.percona.com/blog/the-open-way-of-percona-search-for-mongodb/
